title: Encounters v2
description: The `encounters` block: an index of what travelling thing is near here, at this time of year, and what it is. An index, not a quest generator -- no objectives, stakes, rewards or difficulty, because the consumer that would define them does not exist yet. What it guarantees is that the question is answerable in one lookup rather than a scan over every leg of every group. Version 2 put the answer's own description on the entry: `domain`, `class` and `airborne`. Under version 1 an entry said only which species it was, so "what is near here, on foot" could not be asked of the index -- it meant joining back through beast_movements to beast_nests to drop the water, which on a world three quarters ocean is most of the index.

kind.description: A nomad classification or a creature species id.

threat_tier.description: On the creature-tier rubric so it reads the same as beast_nests. A band takes its tier from its classification: what a band will do to you is a property of what kind of band it is.

domain.description: Where the group lives, on the word key_locations uses for the same idea. A shore species is `land`: the shore medium is refused every water cell, so a traveller can walk to the colony. Flying is not a domain, so `domain == "land"` means reachable on foot.

class.description: What kind of thing it is, on the word wildlife and beast_nests already use. A nomad band is `people`. `kind` is already spent on the species id or the band classification, and the class was lost at the entry.

airborne.description: The species flies. Kept separate from `domain` so a land query does not silently drop roosts a traveller can reach.

occupancy.description: One record per camp a group holds. Camps only: a group in transit is derivable from its leg node path and its speed.
